question: 150 MW at Alviso, San Jose by Jun 2028?
reason: Not 150 MW. Yes to 38.7 MW now.

lanes.name: Grid power
bullets: Transmission plan for 150 MW fails firm N-1 by 45.2 MW.
Needs 111.3 MW beyond distribution capacity.
Thermal and voltage checks pass; N-1 is the blocker.

lanes.name: Edge sites now
bullets: 38.7 MW connectable at distribution, 0% curtailment.
Edge loop proved 16 MW GREEN in round 3.
Directional PG&E GRIP 2028 data, not verified capacity.

lanes.name: Flexibility
bullets: 0% curtailment: 38.8 MW. 2%: 47.6 MW. 10%: 90.6 MW.
Needs a signed storage/curtailment commitment (none today).
Curtailment hours are a contract term, not physics.

lanes.name: Future load
bullets: Edge capacity drops from 38.7 to 7.4 MW.
+20% is an ASSUMED stress case, not a utility forecast.
Lock in capacity early before others queue.

lanes.name: Community consent
bullets: Consent score 0.47 (AMBER band 0.35-0.65). Weights ASSUMED.
San Jose draft standards: recycled-water cooling, carbon-neutral power, generator limits.
Public posts: 83 oppose, 10 support, 17 neutral.

lanes.name: Nature & climate
lanes.text: Refuge beside site; very high flood
bullets: RED: The nearest protected area, Don Edwards San Francisco Bay National Wildlife Refuge, is 0.28 km away.
RED: About 209.8 acres of mapped wetland lie within 500 m, so wetland permits and buffers are likely.
RED: Coastal flooding (storm surge, high tides): FEMA rates the risk for this neighbourhood as very high, a serious issue for this site.

lanes.name: Timeline
bullets: Deadline 2028-06-30: 1.6 years left.
New transmission takes 7-10 years.
Distribution edge sites and storage fit the deadline.
